fix2_applied: Passive scroll listener while a detail is open (startDetailScrollTracking/onDetailScroll/stopDetailScrollTracking, js/main.js ~1082-1120), a y===0-while-tracked->60 guard against the intrinsic zero, closeDetail synchronously stashing window.scrollY before history.back() (~line 1720), exitDetail's first action restoring the stashed value via restoreDetailScroll() (~line 1586), and genuine-back modality defaulting to pointer-like (popstateViaKeyboard defaults false, ~line 1712).
retraction_of_prior_fix1_report: My fix1 verification mis-read two things as bugs that are not: (1) tapping the off-screen .detail-back control from a deep scrollY (e.g. 1069) forces Playwright's own actionability pre-step to scroll the target into view before the click can even dispatch - this is a TEST-METHODOLOGY artifact, not app behaviour: a real touchscreen user physically cannot tap an invisible button either, and .detail-back is a normal in-flow element (not sticky/fixed, confirmed via css/styles.css line 1636), so a real pointer user MUST scroll it into view themselves first, which is a legitimate user-initiated scroll, not a snap. (2) The scrollY change I flagged for Escape exits (landing near 0) is the INTENDED post-morph keyboard focus-into-view behaviour, not a residual bug: it fires at dt~340-380ms after popstate (matching FLIP_MS=340 via focusAfterFlip's setTimeout), i.e. AFTER the morph, not during it; the morph itself (popstate to ~340ms) holds scrollY exactly at its pre-exit value with zero drift at both widths. The landing value is 0 not because of a hardcoded reset but because Chromium's default focus() scroll-into-view centers the newly-focused row in the viewport, and every index row's centering target on this short page computes negative and clamps to 0 - confirmed by focusing a LOWER row (star, the 3rd project) and observing document.activeElement really is the star row post-settle (not a body fallback).
